prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real serving of babi guling at a small Balinese warung in Ubud. The defining feature is the crackling skin: HONEYCOMBED, hundreds of small raised bumps and recessed pits across the surface, 1-5mm bubbles packed tightly, like a piece of golden-brown cork deeply cratered or expanded volcanic pumice that has been fried. The surface is golden-brown to dark mahogany with a thick layer of rendered pork fat glistening between the bumps. The crackle is THICK (3-6mm) and BUMPY, not a thin crust, not a rice-flake batter, not smooth-glazed. Show 2-3 pieces of pork, each with a clear thick bumpy crackle cap on the meat underneath. Served on a banana leaf, with a small mound of white rice, a small saucer of sambal matah (raw shallot + chili + lime + lemongrass), a small heap of lawar (chopped pork with grated coconut + long bean + herbs), wedge of lime. Worn wooden warung table. Glass of es teh in soft background. Soft natural Balinese daylight from the open shopfront, ~40° above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Slightly messy crumb of crackle on the banana leaf. Do NOT render as: babi kecap (sweet-soy glaze), babi goreng kremes (rice-flake batter), babi panggang (smooth-glazed roast), or fried chicken. No microgreens, no fusion garnish, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
